the ingot underwent the HERF process, which involved treatment with a high-speed pneumatic rammer at a pressure of 40 MPa and a speed of 20 m/s
the ingot was heated to 1550 ◦C in a hydrogen atmosphere furnace and then rapidly hot forged along the cylinder axis in air. The initial high cylinder ingot had a reduced thickness of 26 mm.

the forged sample was cut into smaller pieces with the same height but a smaller diameter for the second hit. Instead of employing high temperature as in the previous step, a lower temperature of 1350 ◦C was utilized. After the second strike, the sample thickness decreased to 8.9 mm, demonstrating a height reduction rate of 89.71%.
